finding: t1_build_p0.py's window selection (minute_index <= t0_minute_index + h) always includes the full final minute bucket, whose clock-time end is (60 - offset_into_minute) seconds past the intended t0 + h*60s mark. This is a one-directional look-ahead excess in every horizon's MFE/MAE, present in the whole P0 population, not a data-quality issue in filtered_trades or event_minute_bars_v2 (both confirmed to agree with each other's own content; see t4a's own tick-vs-bar comparison).
why_offset_is_near_zero_for_most_events: D33's tiered t0 construction: 15,259/20,951 events (73%) use the minute_a102 tier, whose t0_ns is built AS the start of a minute bucket by construction -- offset_into_minute ~= 0 for that tier, so the excess is close to the full 60 seconds for most of the population, not a random draw averaging ~30s.
